correctness.rationale: For n=1, the only prescribed set W\{i} is empty and cannot arise from a nonempty action set; for n=2, the neighborhoods {0} and {1} have empty intersection for a joint action. For n>=3, each of n distinct row neighborhoods forces >=n actions per agent. In odd n the off-diagonal arithmetic mean (i+j)/2 modulo n takes every value except i once in row i; its diagonal i+1 repeats an allowed value. For even n, p=n-1 odd finite labels plus infinity, affine midpoint off-diagonal, infinity on finite diagonal, j+1 at infinity cross-entries and 0 at infinity diagonal fill precisely each W\{i}. The construction is exchange-symmetric; all rows and columns have required range, obtaining n^2 profiles. No uniqueness of optimal matrices claimed.
residual_risks: Only two agents, one vetoed outcome per action and deterministic finite outcome sets; no uniqueness or exhaustive classification of optimal matrices.
Finite scripts corroborate, rather than establish, the all-n arithmetic proof.
